diagram_candidates.rationale: The definition is built around the geometric map from the unit square to a triangular domain; a compact diagram would make the image, vertex, and collapsed edge immediately legible alongside the Jacobian.
diagram_candidates.labels_maps_relations: Draw S=[0,1]^2 with r horizontal and s vertical, and T={(x,y):0≤y≤x≤1}. Show D(r,s)=(r,rs), axes/vertices (0,0),(1,0),(1,1), the s=0 and s=1 edges mapping to y=0 and y=x respectively, and the full edge r=0 collapsing to the origin. Label determinant r and state the map has positive orientation for r>0; show no claim of inverse at the collapsed vertex.

diagram_candidates.diagram_kind: Weighted site lifting and lower-hull projection schematic
diagram_candidates.rationale: The definition introduces the three-dimensional regular subdivision by lifting weighted sites into R^4 and projecting lower faces; this geometric construction is difficult to picture from formulas alone.
diagram_candidates.labels_maps_relations: Show a weighted site (p,w) in R^3 mapping to p-hat=(p,||p||^2−w) in R^4. Use a schematic vertical coordinate z=ell(x), mark a lower supporting hyperplane and a lower face, and project its vertices back to a tetrahedral/simplex cell in R^3. Keep the caption explicit that the 4D view is schematic; distinguish the original lift from the fixed-universe lex-refined lift, and do not assert a tetrahedral output on lower-dimensional or degenerate branches.
